notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates, some with the blue EU strip and some fully white; blue strips are more common on the coast and on newer cars.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: White bollards with a black rectangle and a red or white reflector; the top looks like a sharp triangle from above.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Square B-type guardrails, used by only a few European countries.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons have a red arrow on a yellow or white background.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are yellow with a black outline and often a pencil-shaped tip, like those across the former Yugoslavia.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs show a figure with a belt over a 5-stripe zebra; the figure on the northwestern neighbour's sign has no belt.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A Slavic language always written in Latin letters; IJE is common where Serbian uses just E.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Cylindrical concrete or wooden poles, the wooden ones often with alternating hooks.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Exposed red brick walls are seen, more often inland.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Blue fire hydrants with two diagonal protrusions; newer ones have smaller tops but stay blue.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Supermarket chains Konzum and Plodine and the beer brands Karlovačko and Ožujsko show up in ads and shopfronts.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Cars carry HR stickers, mainly older ones before EU plates.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Generation 3 often has a blur that leaves the side mirrors partly visible, sometimes with a small yellow dot on the mirror unique here.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Most generation 3 was shot in autumn, with yellow and orange foliage.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Black and white generation 4 cars that never show an antenna; a generation 2 trekker covers some old town centres.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The northeast is flat farmland like the neighbouring plains to the north and east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The area north and west of the capital is hilly farmland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The coast has rocky mountains, shrubs rather than trees especially in the south, and many islands and peninsulas.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Beige brick houses and walls with green shutters are common along the coast, similar to parts of Italy.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Istria in the northwest sometimes has red soil.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs in two languages, with Italian alongside, are typical of Istria, especially in the west.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Town names ending in -ec are common in the north of the central region.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Lots of vineyards in the far northeast near a town by the Serbian border signal that area.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Only the capital and Osijek have trams; the capital's are blue.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Traffic lights in Rijeka hang from long blue poles extending over the road, exclusive to that city.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Petrinja shows many damaged and ruined buildings from a 2020 earthquake.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Famous preserved medieval city walls visible around the old town in the far south.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall cypress trees are common near the southern tip.
